claim: OCM's central loop (library-driven retrieval: embed query -> top-k memory injection -> generate) materially improves an 8B Q4 local model's output on tasks that depend on prior-session facts, with BOTH retrieval precision and the small model's fact-usage functioning end-to-end on consumer hardware. This is the cheapest discriminating test of the architecture's reason to exist: if memory-ON does not clearly beat memory-OFF here, the persistent-memory differentiator is refuted at small scale.

sanity_check.rationale: If the OFF arm recalls facts it was never given, the corpus is guessable and the run is INVALID, not a confirmation.

workload: corpus.json (65 synthetic prior-session memories across 5 fictional projects + personal prefs; 20 tasks, each with 2-3 exact-matchable key facts)
method_note: Faithful miniature of the Mem0 library-driven retrieval pattern (spec row 9) using Ollama llama3 8B Q4 + mxbai-embed-large cosine top-5 — NOT the OCM binaries. Tests the thesis on the operator's actual hardware class; a CONFIRM justifies standing up the real 3-process OCM stack, a REFUTE kills it before that cost.
source_for_claim: OCM v1 design spec row 9 (library-driven Mem0 retrieval before every turn); README pitch 'remembers everything'
decision_rule: CONFIRM both metrics + sanity green => OCM's core loop is valid at small scale; proceed to Ollama backend adapter + Mem0-on-8B LoCoMo sandbox. REFUTE on fact_recall => 8B cannot use injected memories; thesis fails on target hardware. REFUTE on retrieval => embedding retrieval fails even at toy scale; memory layer needs redesign before any further investment.
